summary: - _“a) Condone the delay in completion of subject assets on merit of the same being out of the control of Petitioner in line with CERC Regulations’2024 22(2) “uncontrollable factors” and approve the tariff as claimed._ - _b) Admit the capital cost as claimed in the Petition and approve the Additional Capitalization incurred / projected to be incurred._ - _d) Allow the petitioner to recover the shortfall or refund the excess Annual Fixed Charges, on account of Return on Equity due to change in applicable Minimum Alternate/Corporate Income Tax rate as per the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended from time to time) of the respective financial year directly without making any application before the Commission as provided in Tariff Regulation 2024 as per para 29 above for respective block._ - _e) Approve the reimbursement of expenditure by the beneficiaries towards petition filing fee, and expenditure on publishing of notices in newspapers in terms of Regulation 94 (1) Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024, and other expenditure (if any) in relation to the filing of the petition._ - _h) Allow the petitioner to claim the overall security expenses and consequential IOWC on that security expenses as mentioned at para 34 above._ - _i) Allow the petitioner to claim the insurance expenses and consequential IOWC on that insurance expenses as mentioned at para 34 above._ - _j) Allow the petitioner to claim the capital spares consumed at the end of tariff block as per actual at para 34 above._ - _k) Allow the petitioner to claim expenses of CTUIL borne by POWERGRID through a separate petition on year to year/ at the end of tariff block as mentioned at para 35 above._ _and pass such other relief as Hon’ble Commission deems fit and appropriate under the circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice”_ 6. The Petitioner has served a copy of the Petition on the Respondents, and notice regarding the filing of this Petition has also been published in the newspapers in accordance with Section 64 of the Act. The Respondent No. 1, Madhya Pradesh Power Management Company Limited (MPPMCL), has filed its reply vide affidavit dated 19.6.2025 and raised objections to the issues of time overrun and Goods and Services Tax (GST). The Petitioner has filed its rejoinder to MPPMCL's reply, vide affidavit dated 5.8.2025. The issues raised by MPPMCL and the clarifications provided by the Petitioner are discussed in the subsequent paragraphs of this order. 7. This order is issued considering the submissions made by the Petitioner in the Petition vide affidavit dated 25.6.2024 and its reply to the Technical Validation (TV) letter vide affidavit dated 16.6.2025; reply filed by MPPMCL vide affidavit dated 19.6.2025, and the Petitioner’s rejoinder to MPPMCL’s reply vide affidavit dated 5.8.2025. The matter was heard on 22.7.2025, and the order was reserved. 8. Having heard the representatives of the Petitioner and perused the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the Petition. 9. The Petitioner has claimed the following transmission charges in respect of the 24. The Respondent, MPPMCL in its reply vide affidavit dated 19.6.2025 has submitted that the reason stated by the Petitioner, i.e. the delay was caused due to the conducting of the Test on the transformer thereby impacting its manufacturing and delivery schedule, does not fall under the category of an uncontrollable event so as to qualify as a “Force Majeure event” or “Change in Law” under Regulation 22 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations and the delay is wholly attributable to the negligence and lack of planning in proper execution of implementation of the transmission asset, on the part of Petitioner. 25. MPPMCL has further submitted that the requirement to conduct the Test on the transformer was a well-known prerequisite imposed by the CEA in April 2021, which was duly amended in September 2021. However, the Petitioner did not raise this issue at the time of approval of the IA. It is submitted that the Petitioner has neither explained the reason for not raising this issue earlier during the IA approval nor provided any facts on record to prove their claim as an uncontrollable event, i.e., a Force Majeure event. It is also submitted that the Petitioner is attempting to unfairly shift the responsibility for the non-execution of the transmission project onto the Respondents, despite being fully aware of the prerequisite condition of the Test for the transformers and voluntarily accepted the SCOD of the transmission asset as 24.11.2023 in the IA. Consequently, the Petitioner cannot now claim ignorance or make claims inconsistent with its prior conscious acceptance of the contractual framework. MPPMCL has submitted that the Petitioner has failed to provide cogent reasons 69. The Petitioner has sought reimbursement of the fee paid by it for filing the Petition and publication expenses. 70. We have considered the Petitioner's submissions. The Petitioner shall be entitled to reimbursement of the filing fees and publication expenses in connection with the present Petition directly from the beneficiaries or long-term customers, as the case may be, on a pro-rata basis in accordance with Regulation 94(1) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. 87. This order disposes of Petition No. 263/TT/2025 in terms of the above findings and discussions.
